newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle trade nil, bids at $71 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle trade nil, bids at $71 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were quiet and expected to remain at a standstill on Tuesday, according to feedlot sources.
Bids were light from $70.00 to $71.00 per cwt, against asking levels of $73.00 to $74.00.
The wide spread between packer bids and asking levels was expected to keep trade slow until midweek when the beef market should be better established, sources said.
Excel Corp, a division of Cargill Inc and IBP Inc last week said they were trimming slaughter starting Monday until their operating margins improve.
The cutbacks were reflected in Monday's estimated cattle slaughter, sources noted.
USDA estimated the day's slaughter at 87,000 head, down from 111,000 a week ago and 120,000 a year ago.
However, potential price weakness from the lighter demand could be offset by tighter supplies of market-ready cattle on this week's showlists.

Trade sources estimated the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma showlist at about 74,000 head, up 1,000 and Kansas was near 56,500, up 2,600. However, sources said many of the cattle on lists were "very green".
